title: Graphene oxide based lamella network for enhanced sound absorption
research_question: To develop an efficient and robust lamella-structure as an acoustic absorber based on self-assembled interconnected graphene oxide (GO) sheets supported by a grill-shaped melamine skeleton, and to investigate its structural, mechanical, acoustic absorption, moisture insulation, and fire-retardant properties.

participants.description: No human participants, material science study.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Graphene oxide (GO) based lamella structures integrated into melamine foam (MF) skeletons, with varying GO loading concentrations resulting in different densities (12.39, 15.68, 18.77, 21.41, 24.12 kg/m³). Reduced GO (rGO) versions were also tested. Control samples were pure melamine foam (9.84 kg/m³). Samples had varying thicknesses (6.5 ± 0.5 mm to 26 ± 0.5 mm).

measures.instrument: Static and dynamic compression tests (load carrying capability, elastic modulus, stiffness, recovery rate)
Water contact angle, moisture absorption/desorption cycles
Burning test (high temperature stability, flammability, self-explosive behavior)

findings.mechanism: Increased tortuosity in wave propagation and enhanced surface area for the GO-based lamella, viscous and thermal losses.
findings.quote: fabricated lamella structure exhibited ~60.3% enhancement over a broad absorption band between 128 Hz and 4000 Hz
The enhanced acoustic absorption is identified to be structure dependent regardless of the density.

findings.antecedent: Increase in GO loading/density (up to 24.12 kg/m³)
findings.consequent: Number of closed cells in porous skeleton
findings.quote: Images confirm the increase in density is related to the increase in the number of closed cells in the porous skeleton

findings.quote: Further increases in the density by increasing the loading of GO deformed the porous structure in size and shape

findings.consequent: Formation of fully closed outer shell covering melamine skeleton
findings.quote: the enhanced loading of nematic-GO in the structure also created a fully closed outer shell covering the entire melamine skeleton
the increase in GO loading increased the mechanical strength of the samples

findings.quote: the flow resistance increased as the sample density increases, which is caused by the increased number of lamella in the structure.

findings.quote: The reduction of GO in MFrGO-3 sample showed higher thermal stability in comparison to the Control-MF and GO modified sample (MFGO-3)

only a single step mass loss was identified for MFrGO-3 sample at 350 °C.

mechanisms: Sound energy dissipation through viscous and thermal losses in porous materials.
Increased tortuosity in wave propagation due to interconnected GO thin film blocking pores.
Enhanced surface area for GO-based lamella.
Improved stiffness of the Control-MF porous skeleton due to internal tension from interconnected GO films.
Creation of an impermeable barrier layer by self-assembled GO lamella sheets to resist moisture penetration.
Reduction of oxygen functional groups in GO structure to provide structural stability and mitigate flammability.
implementation_implications: The developed GO-based lamella structure provides superior structural functionality over conventional sound absorbers, including moisture/mist insulation and fire-retardancy.
The fabrication method is inexpensive, scalable, and adaptable for extensive applications in commercial, residential, and industrial building structures.
The material is suitable for adverse environments including high humidity, under water, and fire risks conditions.
The material is a multifunctional solution for broadband acoustic absorption with potential for noise mitigation in residential, industrial building structures, and transportation systems.

tables.description: Comparison of octave-band acoustic absorption coefficient for our materials with other commercial acoustic absorbers used in building structures.

limitations: The paper does not explicitly state limitations in a dedicated section. However, it notes that excessive GO loading (density > 24.12 kg/m³) leads to structural deformation and undesirable closed outer shells for acoustic applications.

paper_metadata.title: Graphene Oxide‐Based Lamella Network for Enhanced Sound Absorption
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Graphene Oxide‐Based Lamella Network for Enhanced Sound Absorption
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: AbstractNoise is an environmental pollutant with recognized impacts on the psychological and physiological health of humans. Many porous materials are often limited by low sound absorption over a broad frequency range, delicacy, excessive weight and thickness, poor moisture insulation, high temperature instability, and lack of readiness for high volume commercialization. Herein, an efficient and robust lamella‐structure is reported as an acoustic absorber based on self‐assembled interconnected graphene oxide (GO) sheets supported by a grill‐shaped melamine skeleton. The fabricated lamella structure exhibits ≈60.3% enhancement over a broad absorption band between 128 and 4000 Hz (≈100% at lower frequencies) compared to the melamine foam. The enhanced acoustic absorption is identified to be structure dependent regardless of the density. The sound dissipation in the open‐celled structure is due to the viscous and thermal losses, whereas it is predominantly tortuosity in wave propagation and enhanced surface area for the GO‐based lamella. In addition to the enhanced acoustic absorption and mechanical robustness, the lamella provides superior structural functionality over many conventional sound absorbers including, moisture/mist insulation and fire retardancy. The fabrication of this new sound absorber is inexpensive, scalable and can be adapted for extensive applications in commercial, residential, and industrial building structures.
